title: 材料力学Ⅲ
subtitle: Strength of Materials III
educationalGoal: Based on the fundamental knowledge of the relationship between force and deformation in materials studied in the Strength of Materials I and II, students will study the application knowledge required for the design of structures, such as triaxial stresses, strain energy, buckling of column, and so on.
advice: This is a course on strength of materials. We will cover the following topics: 1. Stress-strain relationship under triaxial stress 2. Combination of torsion, bending, and axial forces 3. Strain energy 4. Castigliano's theorem 5. Failure criteria of materials 6. Short column subjected to eccentric load 7. Buckling of long column All of these topics are based on the content learned in "Strength of Materials I": stress, strain, Hook's law, frame structure, thermal stress, stress concentration, thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, a beam and its supporting condition, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam. Students will also need the knowledge learned in "Strength of Materials II": bending stress and deflection in a beam, torsion, principal stress and principal shearing stress, Mohr’s stress circle, and combined stress problems.
books: Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reference books: Basics of Strength of Materials, Baifukan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a good understanding of the content learned in "Strength of Materials I" and "Strength of Materials II. In addition, it is recommended that students understand differential and integral calculation methods, especially for a good understanding of the buckling of a long column.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1. Understand in depth the relationship between stress and strain, and calculate complex combined stress problems. 2. Understand the concept of strain energy, and calculate the deformation of a beam or column using Castigliano's theorem. 3. Explain the different failure criteria for materials. 4. Calculate the stress distribution on a short column subjected to eccentric load, the core of a section, and the buckling load of a long column. 5. Understand the mechanical behavior of materials using mathematical modeling.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. Calculate basic combined stress problems. 2. Calculate strain energy. 3. Understand the failure criteria of materials. 4. Calculate the maximum stress on a short column subjected to eccentric load and the buckling load of long column. 5. Develop mathematical models of materials.
